_doc: PROVISIONAL — inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in Q1 2009: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff (end-2008 state, with 2009 current-year targets that were announced during 2008). Pending verification.
note: Four economies had no headline-CPI target: the Federal Reserve had no numerical target (2.0% is an analytical benchmark), the RBI's objective referred to the wholesale price index, the SARB targeted CPIX, and the Bank of Thailand targeted core inflation; their benchmarks are applied to the headline CPI series used here. China’s benchmark is the government’s annual CPI objective. Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area’s ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: No numerical inflation target. FOMC projections released 19 Nov 2008 (four-year horizon): central tendency for PCE inflation in the outer years 1.4–1.8% and 1.4–1.7%, 'close to or a bit below their assessments of the measured rates of inflation consistent with the Federal Reserve's dual mandate'. 2.0% headline CPI is this monitor's analytical benchmark.
US.index: PCE price index (FOMC projections); benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: FOMC Summary of Economic Projections, 28–29 Oct 2008 meeting (released 19 Nov 2008)

XM.wording: 'A year-on-year increase in the HICP for the euro area of below 2%' … 'maintain inflation rates close to 2% over the medium term' (below but close to 2%: 1.9% used).

urls.label: ECB press release, evaluation of the monetary policy strategy, 8 May 2003

JP.wording: 'Understanding of medium- to long-term price stability' (reviewed April 2008): CPI y/y 'approximately between 0 and 2 percent, with most Policy Board members' median figures at around 1 percent'.

urls.label: BoJ Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices (The Bank's View), 30 Apr 2008

GB.wording: 'The Government's target of 2 per cent for the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI), which applies at all times … The Government stands firmly behind the 2 per cent inflation target' (Pre-Budget Report, 24 Nov 2008).

urls.label: Chancellor's remit for the MPC, 17 Mar 2004
HM Treasury, Pre-Budget Report, November 2008 (Cm 7484), paras 2.77–2.86
Bank of England, exchange of letters regarding CPI inflation, published 16 Dec 2008

CA.wording: Inflation as measured by the CPI at 2 per cent, with a control range of 1 to 3 per cent (renewed November 2006 for five years).

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target: Background Information, Nov 2006

AU.wording: 'Keeping consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over the cycle' (midpoint 2.5%).

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 6 Dec 2007

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: 'The annual change in the consumer price index (CPI) is to be two per cent', tolerance band ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2007:3, October 2007
Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2008:1, February 2008

NO.wording: 'Annual consumer price inflation of approximately 2.5% over time.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 3/07

NZ.wording: Amended Policy Targets Agreement (signed 18 Dec 2008): target unchanged, 'keep future CPI inflation outcomes between 1 per cent and 3 per cent on average over the medium term'; the only change adds a statement of the government's economic objectives.

urls.label: Minister of Finance press release, 'Amended Policy Targets Agreement Signed', 19 Dec 2008 (Scoop)

CN.wording: Government Work Report delivered 5 Mar 2008: 'the rise in the CPI should be held at around 4.8%' (a government objective, not a PBoC target).

urls.label: Report on the Work of the Government, delivered 5 Mar 2008 (NPC English text)
NDRC report on the 2007 plan and 2008 draft plan (NPC English text)

IN.wording: RBI Mid-Term Review: 'the earlier projection of inflation of 7.0 per cent by end-March appears to be valid. It has, therefore, been decided to maintain this estimate for policy purposes', with the endeavour to bring inflation 'below 5 per cent at the earliest' and around 3.0 per cent over the medium term (objective defined on the wholesale price index; no CPI target).
IN.index: WPI; benchmark applied to the CPI series used here

urls.label: RBI Mid-Term Review of Annual Policy for 2008–09, 24 Oct 2008 (para 107)

BR.wording: CMN: 'Fixar para o ano de 2008 a meta para a inflação de 4,5%', tolerance ±2.0 percentage points.

urls.label: CMN Resolution 3,378 of 29 Jun 2006
BCB Inflation Report, December 2007

MX.wording: 'Annual CPI inflation of 3 percent' with a variability interval of ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: IMF Public Information Notice 07/140, Mexico Article IV, 13 Dec 2007
Banxico Inflation Report October–December 2007 and Monetary Program for 2008

ZA.wording: Target band of 3–6 per cent for CPIX (midpoint 4.5%) in force for the current year; the 2008 Medium Term Budget Policy Statement (21 Oct 2008) announced that headline CPI will replace CPIX as the targeted measure from the January CPI of the following year, with the band 'unchanged at 3-6 per cent'.
ZA.index: CPIX until the switch; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: National Treasury, 2008 Medium Term Budget Policy Statement, ch. 2 (A new target measure of inflation), 21 Oct 2008
Minister of Finance, Medium Term Budget Policy Statement speech, 21 Oct 2008

TR.wording: End-2008 CPI inflation target of 4% kept 'for accountability purposes'; the CBRT's open letter to the Government of 3 Jun 2008 proposed raising the targets for the following three years to 7.5%, 6.5% and 5.5%.

urls.label: CBRT No. 2008-14, Open Letter to the Government about inflation targets, 3 Jun 2008
CBRT No. 2008-15, MPC decision of 16 Jun 2008

PL.wording: Continuous CPI target of 2.5% with a ±1 percentage-point tolerance band.

urls.label: NBP Inflation Report, October 2007
NBP Inflation Report, February 2008

HU.wording: 'An inflation rate near the 3 per cent medium term objective.'

urls.label: MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, November 2007
MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, February 2008

CZ.wording: 'The current target of the Czech National Bank (CNB) of 3%' (in effect since January 2006), tolerance ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: CNB press release, 8 Mar 2007

ID.wording: Government inflation target for 2008 of 5% ±1% (set in March 2006, with 8% and 6% for 2006 and 2007).

urls.label: Bank Indonesia Monetary Policy Report, January 2007

KR.wording: Medium-term target of 3.0% ±0.5% on headline CPI inflation for the three years starting 2007, judged on the three-year average (resolution of 17 Aug 2006).

urls.label: Bank of Korea press release, medium-term inflation target, 17 Aug 2006 (redistributed on Newswire)
IMF Country Report 07/344, Korea Article IV, October 2007

CL.wording: 'Keep annual CPI inflation around 3% most of the time, within a tolerance range of plus or minus one percentage point.'

urls.label: Central Bank of Chile, Monetary Policy in an Inflation Targeting Framework, January 2007

CO.wording: Current-year target range 3.5%–4.5% (4% for legal purposes) stands; on 21 Nov 2008 the Board set the following year's target at 4.5%–5.5% with 5% as the point target, and 3% ±1 as the long-run range.

urls.label: Banco de la República press release, 23 Nov 2007 (current-year target)
Banco de la República, Board communiqué, 21 Nov 2008 (following-year target)

TH.wording: 'The MPC uses core inflation (excluding raw food and energy) as its policy target with the range of 0–3.5 per cent (quarterly average)' (midpoint 1.75%).
TH.index: Core CPI; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: BoT Inflation Report, October 2007
BoT Inflation Report, January 2008
